title: Modeling the Carbon Footprint of HPC: The Top 500 and EasyC
problem: HPC carbon emissions are significant for climate change, but accurate carbon accounting for HPC systems is missing. GHG protocol methodologies are difficult to apply to individual systems and infeasible for system collections. No HPC-wide carbon reporting exists.
motivation: Climate change demands accountability and measurement of computational carbon costs. HPC facilities lack standardized carbon reporting, limiting visibility into environmental impact and impeding sustainability efforts.
method: Develops EasyC tool for carbon footprint modeling with limited data availability. Uses publicly available Top500.org data to model operational and embodied carbon for HPC systems. Provides coverage of 391 systems (operational carbon) and 283 systems (embodied carbon). Uses interpolation to estimate carbon footprint for entire Top 500 list. Projects carbon trajectory through 2030.
key_novelty: First comprehensive carbon footprint assessment of Top 500 HPC systems; EasyC tool enabling carbon modeling with minimal data requirements; projection methodology for future carbon impact.
contributions: EasyC tool for simplified carbon footprint modeling
Operational and embodied carbon assessment methodology
Coverage of 391 systems operational carbon, 283 systems embodied carbon
First carbon footprint estimates of Top 500 systems
limitations: Data availability limits direct measurement for many systems
Embodied carbon estimation less complete (80.8%) than operational (98%)
Interpolation methodology assumptions not detailed in abstract
Specific Top 500 systems and their carbon profiles not discussed
Uncertainty bounds and confidence intervals not provided
Future projections dependent on unspecified assumptions
